attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, node3 (standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04. Created a dedicated cluster CA on node1, issued server certs (CN=nodeX, SAN DNS/IP) for each node and one client cert (CN=replicator) for the replication role, deployed them to each node's data directory / postgres home. Enabled ssl=on with ssl_ca_file on all nodes, and restricted replication access in pg_hba.conf to `hostssl replication replicator <cluster-ip>/32 cert clientcert=1` — no other pg_hba rule matches replication connections, so plaintext or uncertified peers are rejected. Bootstrapped node2/node3 via pg_basebackup over TLS with sslmode=verify-full using the replicator client cert, configured recovery.conf with matching sslmode=verify-full/sslcert/sslkey/sslrootcert, and confirmed both standbys stream from node1 with pg_stat_ssl.ssl=t. Verified end-to-end data replication (INSERT on primary visible on both standbys) and proved cert-authority enforcement by attempting a connection with a self-signed (non-CA) cert bearing CN=replicator, which was rejected at the TLS handshake ('tlsv1 alert unknown ca'). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id/uptime and health baselines, restarted node2, node3, then node1 (primary last, preserving write availability as long as possible) one at a time via `systemctl reboot` with the acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled each node until reachable, confirmed each node's boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, and verified PostgreSQL auto-restarted, replication state recovered (pg_is_in_recovery, pg_stat_replication streaming/async, ssl=t) and that a post-restart write on the primary replicated to both standbys.
